purpose: This medication is used to treat chronic hepatitis B and chronic hepatitis C, which are viral infections that affect the liver. It helps your body fight the virus and can reduce liver damage over time. It is sometimes used alone or in combination with other antiviral medicines.
how_it_works: Your body naturally makes a protein called interferon to help fight infections. This medicine is a man-made version of that protein, designed to last longer in your body. It works by boosting your immune system and directly slowing down the virus so it cannot multiply as easily.
common_side_effects: Many people feel flu-like symptoms such as tiredness, fever, chills, headache, and muscle aches, especially after the injection. You may also notice nausea, loss of appetite, hair thinning, or mood changes like feeling sad or irritable. Injection site redness or soreness is also common.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious mood changes, including depression and thoughts of self-harm, so tell your doctor right away if you feel very sad or have unusual thoughts. It can lower your blood cell counts, making it harder to fight infection or causing bruising and bleeding. It should NOT be used during pregnancy as it can harm the baby, and reliable birth control is required. Regular blood tests are needed to monitor your liver, blood counts, and thyroid function while on this medicine.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous) once a week. The usual dose for adults is 180 micrograms injected once every week. Treatment typically lasts 24 to 48 weeks depending on your condition and how well you are responding. Your doctor or nurse will show you how to give yourself the injection at home.
